title: Stakeholder Signal Exchange & Priority Fungibility
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: top-account requests and executive escalations arrive via many channels (CS, AE, support, CSMs, sales ops). We lack a consistent broker that translates stakeholder signals into fungible, auditable prioritization tokens that product and engineering can consume in sprint planning. This results in: ad-hoc cut-ins, missed SLAs, and opaque promises to customers.

Goal: design and deliver a lightweight 'Signal Exchange'—an intake + adjudication + credit system that: (1) normalizes multi-source customer signals into a single priority token, (2) exposes a simple marketplace where PMs can reserve sprint-credit against tokens, (3) provides automated audit logs and SLA anchors for VP/Customer escalations. The system should integrate with Linear for ticket gating, Console for telemetry (latency/cost dashboards), and Salesforce for commercial alignment.
acceptance_criteria: Signal payload schema defined and documented in Confluence (source, impact metric, justification, customer tier, request ETA)
Signal adjudication ruleset prototype implemented (auto-accept, require-review, reject) with test vectors
Linear integration: signals create gated Linear tickets with priority_token and SLA fields populated
Sprint-credit marketplace UI mock in Figma and functioning reserve API for PMs to allocate credits
Audit log generated for each adjudication event in Console with customer_id, actor, rule, and outcome
Pilot run with two strategic accounts and Success/Commercial signed off on handoff runbook
decision_log: 2025-01-20: Decided to normalize inbound signals into a 5-point impact scale rather than raw revenue buckets (favored signal comparability across deals) — agreed by GTM and PM leadership
2025-01-28: Chose to represent priority tokens as opaque strings stored on Linear tickets instead of creating an external ledger service (reduced infra scope)
2025-02-10: Agreed on eligibility: only accounts with ARR >= threshold or active escalation SLA can mint high-priority tokens — fallback path for mid-market via CSM review
2025-02-18: Opted to postpone complex marketplace economics (credits buy fractional scope) to phase 2; phase 1 will support fixed sprint-credit reservations

risks: Promise creep: without strict guardrails, commercial teams may over-request priority tokens leading to missed SLAs
Operational load: adjudication step could create latency in response to escalations if humans are required for most decisions
Integration complexity with Salesforce could create sync issues and mismatched customer expectations
Audit / retention policy might conflict with enterprise legal/regulatory requirements without explicit opt-outs
